title: A captioned arrow sits right: tight selection, a pill that follows the drag, a tail that touches
goal: The arrow with a caption is nearly right and four things spoil it. Its selection box is far bigger than the arrow and pill together, so a small arrow looks like it owns half the screen. Grabbing the tail makes the pill vanish for the whole drag, so you cannot see where the label will end up until you let go. The tail stops a few pixels short of what it points at, leaving a visible gap instead of touching. And the tail often does not meet the pill at all: it ends off to one side with a space between them, when it should run into the middle of the pill's near edge.
notes: Reported by the user on 2026-09-05 with a screenshot, three separate causes found by reading. (1) Selection box: AnnotationBuilder in Tools.swift builds the frame as the drag box inset by renderPadding, then unions it with the caption pill rect inset again by captionShadowPadding. One rectangle spanning an arrow and a pill that hangs off its tail is mostly empty, and the selection outline draws that frame. The frame itself has to stay big enough to render into, so the fix is in what the selection DRAWS: hug the arrow and the pill as two shapes or as their tight union, not the padded frame. (2) Pill vanishing: CanvasView.refreshEndpointPreview at line 3649 calls displayAnnotationPreview, which draws the annotation vectors and no caption at all; only the commit path, EditorState.commitAnnotationEndpoints, calls AnnotationBuilder.planningCaption. Replan and draw the pill in the live preview so the drag shows the truth. (3) Tail gap: not diagnosed, measure it first. Suspects to check rather than assume: the line cap and stroke width moving the visual end away from the endpoint, and renderPadding. The user says a handful of pixels, so measure in document points at two zooms before changing anything. (4) Tail not meeting the pill, reported with a second screenshot on 2026-09-05 showing a short label ok whose pill is nearly circular, with the tail ending above and left of it and a clear space between. Suspect, to be measured rather than assumed: CaptionPlanner in AnnotationEditing.swift around line 385 places the pill by an ATTACHMENT POINT, and its default candidate is tail plus the shaft direction times captionGap (6pt, Layer.swift line 194), while the other candidates sit squarely left, right, above or below the tail. attachment(forPillCenter:) converts a centre to that attachment. If the conversion assumes the near side is one of four flat edges of a rectangle, a diagonal shaft will attach nearer a corner than the true near point, which both offsets it and opens a gap, and a nearly circular pill makes it obvious. Fix the geometry so the attachment is the point where the shaft line crosses the pill's rounded outline, and keep the 6pt gap as a deliberate breathing space or drop it, whichever looks connected.
acceptance: The selection shown for a captioned arrow hugs what is actually drawn, the arrow and its pill, with no wide empty margin around either
Dragging either end keeps the pill on screen the whole time, re-placed live where it will land, so letting go changes nothing you can see
The tail meets what it points at with no gap, at every zoom and every stroke width, checked against a straight edge in a picture
The tail runs into the middle of the pill's near edge and touches it, for a short label whose pill is nearly round and for a long one, and at every angle including diagonals
Nothing about where a committed arrow or pill sits changes beyond these corrections, so an existing document only gets better
Core logic covered by tests in PhotonzCore written before the implementation, including a case at several angles and several label lengths

Audit written under queue/audits/ with pictures of a selected captioned arrow, a tail mid drag, a tail against a border at two zooms, and a short label at four angles, anything rough filed as a follow-up
